overall: The AG found the Carver Planning Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law: it declined a broad audit of a year of minutes, found the sampled minutes listed documents, and found the complaint-review steps satisfied the law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged that planning board minutes from January 2021 to February 2022 omit the list of documents used at meetings, as the Open Meeting Law requires.
allegations.key_passage: We decline to review an entire year of meeting minutes to determine whether they contain a list of documents as our office will not conduct broad audits of public bodies based on generalized allegations.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the board's minutes lack a list of documents used. The AG reviewed the January, February 8 and February 22, 2022 minutes sampled.
allegations.key_passage: Nevertheless, we did review minutes of Board meetings that occurred in January and February of 2022 (January 25, February 8, and February 22) and note that these three sets of meeting minutes include a list of documents used during each meeting.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the chair refused to state publicly the substance of prior Open Meeting Law complaints, and the board did not follow proper complaint-response procedure.
allegations.key_passage: While we acknowledge that the Board did not substantively discuss the allegations raised in the complaints, the Open Meeting Law does not require a public body to engage in a substantive discussion of the merits of each complaint, nor to read a complaint in full during a meeting.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
